agiraffedog: Otto "Ghost" Agiraffedog reported to S-S10 with a bullet that missed him sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
The dugout roof dripped into Otto "Ghost" Agiraffedog's mug. He moved the mug. The roof found another way.
The machine gun jammed at the worst moment. Otto "Ghost" Agiraffedog cleared it with a bent nail and words the chaplain pretended not to hear.
hunter_dorf0629: Konrad Dorf arrived on Day 6 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
Someone had labelled the water bucket 'Soup'. Konrad Dorf changed it back after lunch, too late to settle the argument.
newnario: On the way to R-F17, Viktor Newnario tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.
The Concord took Verdel Ridge. Viktor Newnario watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
Dawn watch. Viktor Newnario put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Tobias "Shadow" Hawkenram, grazed.
The party came back from Sorrow Copse by different routes. By dawn, everyone had been accounted for except Viktor Newnario.

The missing report was still on the desk when Viktor Newnario walked in. The clerk crossed it out hard enough to tear the paper. Victory at Hill 304. Viktor Newnario let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.
An old advertisement showed a spotless man smoking beside a fireplace. Viktor Newnario added a leak above the man's head in pencil.
Viktor Newnario and Clement Jewnipers carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.
the_ghost_of_sky: Severin Sky arrived at R-F9 with a carefully folded uniform. The first low beam corrected the cap; the first puddle corrected the rest.
Felix Varsikasikra taught Severin Sky to play the harmonica. The bay has asked them both, formally, to stop.
Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Severin Sky stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
Severin Sky got a photo of the family house. He spent longer looking at the strange curtains than at the faces.

Severin Sky had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Jonas Miked crossed it, Severin Sky fired. Jonas Miked was badly wounded. A shell landed square in R-F9. They found Severin Sky alive under the sandbags, barely. Every minute counts now. Severin Sky died at his post at R-F9 when the dugout roof came down under a direct hit.
The House of Sky sent Casimir Sky after Severin Sky. This time the family packed two pairs of spare socks.

Casimir Sky washed his face and someone asked if headquarters was visiting. Apparently being clean needs an explanation. The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Casimir Sky did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
A bullet went through Casimir Sky's sleeve at R-F9 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Zeno "Ghost" Kattawar of the Concord (@max.kattawar).
A single shot from across the wire hit Casimir Sky in the thigh at R-F9. He crawled the last yards on his elbows. Shot by Matthias Mart of the Concord (@frank_mart00).
vitocarcioppolo: Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp arrived on Day 4 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.

Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp kept watch so that Norbert Seamus could sleep. Then Norbert kept watch so that Mole could. Neither slept. Mail came up the line with a letter for Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp. Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp spent the night in no man's land with pliers and a roll of wire. Every flare meant lying flat in the mud. The gap at S-F19 is closed now. A clear shot from S-F19. Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp grazed Norbert Cheese and slid back down below the parapet. Hill 304 is lost. Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
Leopold Moodie fixed the strap on Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp's pack. The price was a biscuit and a promise to stop mentioning the haircut.
Casimir "Mole" Vitocarciopp found a shirt button in the bread. He ate around it and kept the button. Both were useful.
